basics.name: Jared Seto
basics.label: Student
basics.summary: I am currently pursuing a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Computer Science through the Department of Information and Computer Sciences at the University of Hawaiʻi. My academic journey has equipped me with a strong foundation in computational theory, software development, and emerging technologies. I am committed to applying the knowledge gained throughout my studies to solve real-world challenges, contribute to innovative projects, and make a meaningful impact in the tech industry. I am set to graduate in Spring 2026 and look forward to gaining hands-on experience through internships, research opportunities, and collaborative projects that will further develop my technical skills and professional network.

work.summary: Managed daily operations of a 20+ workstation computer lab serving ~500 student-athletes and faculty weekly, ensuring a productive and accessible environment.
highlights: (1) Maintained and regularly updated the SAAS website using WordPress, ensuring real-time accuracy of academic resources.
(2)  Responded promptly to tech support requests, diagnosing and resolving issues related to Windows OS, academic software, and network access using built-in admin tools and user guidance.
(3) Updated operating systems and academic software (e.g., Microsoft Office, web browsers), and performed disk cleanups and user account resets to maintain reliable computer performance.

work.summary: Handled student and faculty inquiries related to scheduling, forms, and career services, resolving issues directly or coordinating with staff to ensure timely support.
highlights: (1) Managed front desk duties including appointment scheduling, phone coverage, and resource distribution for students and faculty.
(2) Coordinated with recruiters to schedule interview rooms and set up digital sign-up sheets using Excel and the university's online career platform.
(3) Helped coordinate logistics for career fairs and workshops, including setup, registration, and on-site support for 100+ student attendees.

awards.title: Hawai'i Annual Code Challenge Finalist
awards.summary: The HACC is an annual event that solicits challenges from state departments and community groups and asks student, amateur and professional coders to develop technology applications to help solve specific problems. In 2024, 17 teams advanced as finalists out of a total of 41 participating teams.

awards.title: Dean's List
awards.summary: Undergraduate students are awarded the Dean’s List distinction if they: (1) earn a semester grade point average of 3.5 or higher based on 12 credits or more taken for a grade (C/NC courses do not count), and (2) do not receive grades of W, I, F, or NC for that semester.

awards.title: Academic Honors
awards.summary: Awarded to students that graduate with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above and completed 4 credits of math, 4 credits of science, and 2 credits from AP/IB/Running Start courses.

awards.title: CTE Honors
awards.summary: Awarded to students that graduate with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above and completed a two-course sequence in an approved CTE program or program of study with a B or better and met or exceeded proficiency on a performance-based assessment.
